Tests remain active until they reach an expiry condition you define. By default, a test invitation has **Never** expiry, meaning it stays active indefinitely. You can set a custom expiry date or define a start‑and‑end window, after which the test is considered expired and candidates can no longer access it.

## Steps to view or change test active period
1. Open the test in the **Tests** dashboard.
2. Click **Invite Candidates** (or edit the test settings).
3. Locate the **Expiry** dropdown.
4. Choose an option:
   - **Never** – test stays active forever (default).
   - **Custom** – select a specific expiry date, time, and time zone, then click **Save**.
5. (Optional) To define a start and end window, go to **Modify Test Expiration Time** in the test settings and set the desired start/end times, then save.

## Notes
- After the expiry date passes, invited candidates cannot access the test, the **Invite** button is disabled, and you cannot send new invitations.
- Restoring an archived test re‑enables candidate invites, but the test will still respect any expiry settings you have configured.

Hi,


Consider these guidelines when choosing between creating a new test or a variant:



When to Use Test Variants:

Create variants to adapt a single test to different candidate profiles, 
such as roles with different tech stacks (React, Angular, Vue.js).
Variants streamline assessments by showing candidates only relevant sections and generating role-specific reports.


Advantages of Test Variants:

Reduces the need to manage multiple tests, improving efficiency.
Decreases maintenance while allowing scalable personalization.
Ensures candidates are tested on relevant content.


Disadvantages and Limitations of Test Variants:

A test must have at least two variants to function; you cannot delete a variant if only two exist.
Variants without logic are hidden from candidates until logic is added.
detailed_results.predicted_response:
## Overview
Creating a **test variant** lets you reuse a single test while delivering role‑specific sections based on a candidate’s input. A separate test should be used when the assessment content is fundamentally different and cannot be expressed as variations of a common core.

## Key Points
- **When to use a variant**: You have a core assessment that applies to multiple roles (e.g., front‑end developer) and only need to swap out language‑specific or framework‑specific questions.
- **When to create a new test**: The skill set, difficulty, or overall structure differs enough that a shared core would add unnecessary complexity (e.g., a back‑end systems design test vs. a front‑end UI test).

## Advantages of Variants
- Deliver the appropriate version automatically at login, reducing manual test selection.  
- Reports reflect only the variant attempted, keeping insights clean and role‑specific.  
- Maintenance overhead is lower because you manage one test with shared sections instead of multiple independent tests.  
- Supports scaling assessments across many tech stacks with a single streamlined setup.

## Limitations
- A variant‑based test **requires at least two variants** (Document 1).  
- Managing multiple variants can add configuration complexity compared to a single test.

## Best Practices
1. Identify a common core (e.g., coding fundamentals) that all roles share.
2. Create separate variants for each technology stack or role‑specific focus.
3. Use the **Add New Skill Bundle** or **Add from Other Variants** buttons to reuse questions across variants (Document 3).
4. If you anticipate only one version, create a dedicated test instead of a variant.

## Reference
- [Create Test Variants](https://support.hackerrank.com/articles/7530103378-test-variants)
- [July 2025 Release Notes – Test Variants](https://support.hackerrank.com/articles/3121307537-july-2025-release-notes)

Candidates see only the sections relevant to them, and reports reflect just the variant they attempted, so insights stay clean, role-specific, and easy to evaluate. This reduces maintenance overhead while giving you the flexibility to personalize assessments at scale.

For more information, see [📄 Test Variants](/articles/7530103378).

Subscription plans

**What happens if I exceed my new plan’s limits during a downgrade transition?**

You continue to have access to your current plan features and credits (Entitlements included in your subscription) until the cycle ends, even if your usage exceeds the new plan’s limits.

**Do I get a refund when I upgrade mid-cycle?**

No. You pay the prorated difference for the upgrade and gain immediate access to new features.

**Can I change from monthly to quarterly billing without changing my plan tier?**

Yes. HackerRank treats this as an upgrade. The change takes effect immediately with prorated billing.

**What happens to my unused credits when I upgrade?**

HackerRank forfeits all unused credits from your previous plan. You immediately receive the full credit allocation of your new plan.

**What should I do if I accidentally click Start Test and lose a credit?**

When you click **Start Test**, the system immediately records your attempt. However, you do not lose access to the test. You can return and continue from where you left off at any time.

## Overview
You can give a candidate additional time and then send them a new invitation. The extra time is added first; if the test is already completed or uses DevOps questions, you must reinvite them for a fresh attempt.

## Prerequisites
- Access to a **HackerRank for Work** account with permission to edit tests.
- The candidate must already appear in the **Candidates** tab of the test.

## Steps
1. **Log in** to HackerRank for Work.
2. Navigate to the **Tests** tab and open the relevant test.
3. Click the **Candidates** tab.
4. Locate the candidate (use filters if needed) and tick the checkbox next to their name.
5. Click **More > Add Time**.
6. Enter the additional minutes (e.g., 53) and press **Confirm**.
   - *Note*: If the candidate is currently taking the test, they must refresh the page to see the new timer. If they have already finished, they will need to log in again.
7. After adding time, keep the candidate selected and click **More > Re‑invite** (or the **Reinvite** button).
8. Review the invitation email content; the duration shown will reflect the original test length, but the extra minutes are now applied to the candidate’s session.
9. Click **Send Invite**.

## Notes
- Do **not** add time to a DevOps‑based test after the candidate has submitted; the VM is purged and extra time won’t restore access. In that case, simply reinvite the candidate for a new attempt.
- The candidate can accept the new invite at any time; you do not need to delete the previous attempt.

- Adding extra time: https://support.hackerrank.com/articles/4811403281-adding-extra-time-for-candidates

Adding extra time

To add extra time for specific candidates:

1. Log in to your **HackerRank for Work** account using your credentials.

2. Go to the **Tests** tab. 

3. Select the test you want to modify.

4. Go to the **Candidates** tab.

5. Select the checkbox next to the candidate(s).

6. Click **More > Add Time. **

7. Enter the time in minutes.

8. Click **Confirm**.

**Note: **

- A candidate who is still in a test session must refresh the page to see the updated timer.

- A candidate who has completed the test must log in again to view the added time.

- Do not add time to a test that contains DevOps questions after it ends or after the candidate submits it. The system purges the virtual machine for DevOps questions upon submission, and added time does not restore access. To allow additional time, re-invite the candidate to take the test as a new attempt.

Adding extra time in variant-based tests

For variant-based tests, you can add extra time at the section level for candidates.

To add extra time for specific candidates in a variant-based test:

1. Log in to your **HackerRank for Work** account using your credentials.

2. Go to the **Tests** tab. 

3. Select the test you want to modify.

4. Go to the **Candidates** tab.

5. Select the checkbox next to one or more candidates from the same test variant.

6. Click **More > Add Time. **

7. In the **Add additional time** dialog, enter additional time (in minutes) for the required sections.

8. Click **Confirm**.

**Note:**

- The **Add additional time** dialog displays only the sections included in the selected variant (for example, Problem Solving, JavaScript, or CSS).

- For bulk updates, select candidates from the same test variant. If you select candidates from different variants, the **Add time** option is disabled. Filter the candidate list to a single variant to continue.

- Candidates who are actively taking the test must refresh the page to see the updated timer.

- Candidates who have completed the test must log in again to view the added time.

Modifying test expiration time

To modify the test expiration time:

1. Log in to your **HackerRank for Work** account using your credentials.

2. Go to the **Tests** tab.

3. Open the test you want to update.

4. Go to **Settings > General**.

5. Modify the **Start date & time** and **End date & time** in the **Test Expiration Time** section.

6. Click **Save Changes**.

 **Note:** 

 - By default, the **Test Expiration Time** fields are empty.

 - To restore the default state, click the clear icon (**X**) to remove the **Start date & time** and **End date & time** values.

**Note**: 

If a candidate needs to retake a test, you can reinvite them at any time. You do not need to delete the previous invite or attempt. For more information, see [📄 Reinvite Candidates to a Test](/articles/1002936098).

8. Enter your **account password**.

You can permanently remove a conversation (or multiple conversations) that contain private information from your Claude chat history.

## Overview
You purchased Visa Traveller’s Cheques from Citicorp and they were stolen in Lisbon. To protect yourself and recover the value, you need to report the loss to the issuing bank and request a refund.

## Prerequisites
- The cheque serial numbers
- Proof of purchase (date, location, amount)
- Details of when and where the cheques were stolen
- The name of the issuing bank (Citicorp)

## Steps
1. **Contact the issuing bank immediately** – call Citicorp’s fraud‑loss line (or use the contact details on your receipt). If you cannot locate Citicorp’s number, call Visa’s free‑phone line for traveller’s cheques: see the “Contact us” link in the Visa traveller’s cheques page.
2. **Provide the required information**:
   - Cheque serial numbers
   - Purchase details (where and when you bought them)
   - Circumstances of the loss (date, location, how they were stolen)
   - Confirmation that Citicorp is the issuer
3. **Request a refund** – the issuer will process the refund, typically within 24 hours, subject to terms and conditions.
4. **Follow up** – keep a record of the call reference number and any email confirmation. If the refund is delayed, contact Visa’s travel support using the free‑phone number listed on the traveller’s cheques support page.

## Notes
- Acting quickly reduces the risk of fraudulent use.
- Refund eligibility depends on the issuer’s terms; having all required details speeds the process.
